6271	12.3 插入和删除
6272	插人和删除操作会引起由二叉搜索树表示的动态集合的变化。一定要修改数据结构这个变化，但修改要保持二叉搜索树性质的成立。正如下面将看到的，插入一个新结点带修改要相对简单些，而删除的处理有些复杂。
6273	插入
6274	要将一个新值v插入到一棵二叉搜索树T中，需要调用过程TREE-INSERT。该过和z作为输人，其中z.key=v,z.left=NIL,z.right=NIL。这个过程要修改T和z的某来把z插人到树中的相应位置上。
6275	TREE-INSERT(T,z)
6276	1 y=NILMUPI
6277	3 while x≠ NIL
6278	y=x
6279	ifz.key<ky
6280	x=x.left
6281	elseHright

10452	Exercise: Given an array of items A=(a0,...,an-1), describe a O(n)-time algorithm to con-struct a binary tree T containing the items in A such that (1) the item stored in the ith node of T's traversal order is item a;, and (2) T has height O(logn).
10453	Solution: Build T by storing the middle item in a root node, and then recursively building the remaining left and right halves in left and right subtrees. This algorithm satisfies property (1) by definition of traversal order, and property (2) because the height roughly follows the recurrence H(n) = 1+ H(n/2). The algorithm runs in O(n) time because every node is recursed on once doing constant work.

10459	if i < c:

15802	Recitation 6
15803	Exercise: Given an array of items A = (ao,.,an-1), describe a O(n)-time algorithm to con-struct a binary tree Tcontaining the items in A such that (1) the item stored in the ith node of T's traversal order is item ai, and (2) T has height O(log n).
15804	Solution: Build T by storing the middle item in a root node, and then recursively building the remaining left and right halves in left and right subtrees. This algorithm satisfies property (1) by definition of traversal order,and property (2) because the height roughly follows the recurrence H(n)=1+H(n/2). The algorithm runs in O(n) time because every node is recursed on once doing constant work.
15805	: def build(X):
15806	A = [x for x in X]
15807	def build_subtree(A, i, j):
15808	c=(i+j)//2
15809	root = self.Node_Type(A[c])
15810	if i<c:
15811	root.left=build_subtree(A, i, c -1)
15812	root.left.parent =root
15813	if c < j:
15814	root.right -build_subtree(A, c+1,j)
15815	root.right.parent =root
15816	self.root= build_subtree(A, 0, len(A)-1)
15817	return root

15920	if i < c:                            # 左边还有元素

15923	if c < j:                            # 右边还有元素

29363	----G" Iacs on uie logn Kevengers having
29364	the strongest opinions (breaking ties arbitrarily), so he can meet with them to discuss. For this problem, assume that the record containing the polls is read-only access controlled (the material in classified), so any computation must be written to alternative memory.
29365	(a) Describe an O(n)-time algorithm to generate Fick's list.
29366	Solution: Build a maximum priority queue containing all Revengers (together with their names). The priority queue stores at most n Revengers, so should take up no more than O(n) space. Key each Revenger r; with opinion s; on the pair (|sil,i) to make keys unique. Then delete the maximum keyed Revenger log n times and return the results. The running time of this algorithm is B(n) + (log n).D where B(n) is the time to build a priority queue of size n and D is the time for delet max. We can achieve the desired running time by using a binary max-heap as our priority queue,since build takes O(n) time and deletions take amortized O(log n) time.
29367	(b) Now suppose Fick's computer is only allowed to write to at most O(logn) space.Describe an O(n log log n)-time algorithm to generate Fick's list.
29368	Solution: Build a minimum priority queue containing the opinions of the first log n Revengers in the list (together with their names). Key each Revenger r; with opinion s, on the pair (|sil, i) to make keys unique. Then repeat the following procedure for the remaining Revengers, while maintaining the invariant that after processing Revenger i, the priority queue contains the log n Revengers from the first i having the highest absolute opinion, which is true for i = log n and would solve our problem when i = n:(1) delete the minimum Revenger r* from the priority queue, (2) compare the key of r*to that of the ith Revenger ri, and (3) insert whichever is larger into the priority queue.Ifr; <r", then r; is smaller than every Revenger in the priority queue so is not in the top log n. Alternatively, if r* < ri, then ri is larger than the k:th largest found so far. In either case, adding the larger to the priority queue maintains the invariant. In all cases,the priority queue stores at most logn Revengers, so should take up no more than O(log n) space. The running time of this algorithm is B(log n)+(n-log n).(I+D)where B(log n) is the time to build a priority queue of size log n and I and D are the time for insertion and delete min respectively. Thus we can use either a Set AVL tree or a min-heap as our priority queue to achieve O(n log log n) running time, using at most O(log n) space.

29956	Problem 4-3. SCLR
29957	Stormen, Ceiserson, Livest, and Rein are four academics who wrote a very popular textbook in computer science,affectionatelyknown as SCLR. They just found &: first editions in their offices,and want to auction them off online for charity. Each bidder in the auction has a unique integer randcanidsomepositive integer amount for a single copy (but may increase or decrease their bid while the auction is live). Describe a database supporting the following operations, as-suming n is the number of bidders in the database at the time of the operation. For each operation,state whether your running time is worst-case, expected, and/or amortized.
29958	new_bid(d, b)
29959	record a new bidder ID d with bid b in O(log n) time
29960	update_bid(d, b)
29961	update the bid of existing bidder ID d to bid b in O(log n) time
29962	get_revenue()
29963	return revenue from sellingtothecurrentk highest bidders in O(1) time Solution: First, observe that operation update_bid requires finding and modifying the bid of a bidder given their ID, so maintain a dictionary containing the bidders keyed by bidder ID (call it the bidder dictionary). Either a hash table or Set AVL tree will work for this purpose, where using a hash tablewill yield amortized expected running times for the first two operations.We will also need to keep track of an ordering of bids stored: in particular the sum of the k highest at any given time. To do this, maintain two priority queues: a min priority queue containing the k: highest bids, and a max priority queue containing the remaining n-I: bids. Because we need O(log n) performance on priority queue insertions or deletions, we can use either Set AVL trees or binary heaps to implement the priority queues, where using binary heaps will yield amortized running times for the first two operations.
29964	In order to find where each bidder is in the priority queues, we store with each bidder in the bidder dictionary a cross-linking pointer to the bidder's bid in one of the priority queues (i.e., its AVL node or index in a binary heap). In what follows, we will assume a Set AVL tree is used to implement the bidder dictionary and the priority queues. In addition, maintain the sum B of all bids in the min priority queue so that we can return it in constant time.
29965	To implement newbidd,b),emovthmallest bidwith bidder ID d' from the min priority queue in O(log n) time, and decrease B by its bid amount '. Then compare b to b'. Whichever is larger is among the k highest bidders seen so far while the other is not, so insert the larger into the min priority queue in O(log n) time while increasing B by its bid; and insert the smaller into the max priority queue, also in O(log n) time. In addition, add d to the bidder dictionary pointing to its bid location in a priority queue, and update the pointer associated with bidder d'. each in O(logn)time. This procedure maintains the invariants of the data structures presented, and runs in O(log n)total time in the worst case.
29966	To implement update_bid (d, b), find existing bidder d's bid location in the priority queues using the bidder dictionary in O(logn) time, and then remove its record from its priority queue,also in O(logn) time. If the min priority queue has only k: - 1 bids, remove the max from the max priority queue and insert it into the min priority queue in O(logn) time. While doing this.recompute B in O(1) time and update the cross-linked pointers in O(logn) time. Now that the bidder with ID d has been removed, we can now reinsert it as a new bidder with updated bid b and

32192	record p points for jersey r in game g
32193	clear(g, r)
32194	remove any record that jersey r played in game g
32195	ranked_receiver (k)
32196	return the jersey with the kth highest performance
32197	Solution: First. observe that operations require finding and modifying records for a receiver given a jersey number in O(logn) time, so maintain dictionary containing the receivers keyed by unique jersey(call it thejerseydictionary).Since we need to achieve worst-case O(log n) running time,we cannot afford the expected performance of a hash table, so we implement the dictionary using a Set AVL tree.
32198	For each receiver, we will need to find and update their games by game ID, so for each receiver in the jersey dictionary, we will maintain a pointer to their own Set AVL tree containing that receiver's games keyed by game ID (call this a receiver's game dictionary). With each receiver's game dictionary, we will maintain the number of games they've played and the total number of points they've scored to date. We can compare the performance of two jerseys from their respective number of games and points via cross multiplication.
32199	Lastly, to find the kth highest performing receiver, we maintain a separate Set AVL tree on the receivers keyed by performance, augmenting each node with the size of its subtree (call this the performance tree). We showed in lecture how to maintain subtree size in O(1) time, so we can maintain this augmentation. Each node of the jersey dictionary will store a cross-linking pointer to the node in the performance tree corresponding to that player. Since we use Set AVL trees for all data structures, Set operations run in worst-case O(log n) time.
32200	To implement record(g, r, p), find player r's game dictionary D in the receiver dictionary in O(log n) time. If game g is in D, update its stored points to p in O(log n) time and update the total number of points stored with r's game dictionary in O(1) time. Otherwise, insert the record of game g into D in O(logn) time, and update the number of games and total points stored in O(1) time The performance of r may have changed, so find the node corresponding to r in the performance tree, remove the receiver's performance from the tree, update its performance, and then reinsert into the tree all in O(logn) time. This operation maintains the semantics of our data structures in worst-case O(log n) time.Problem Session 4
32201	To implement clear(g, r),find playerr's game dictionary D in the receiver dictionary as before and remove g (assuming it exists).Identically to above, maintain the stored number of games and total points, and update th performance tree together in worst-case O(log n) time.To implement ranked_receiver (k), find the kth highest performance in the performance tree by using the subtree size augmentation: if the size of a node's right subtree is k or larger,recursively find in the right subtree; if the size of the node's right subtree is k-1, then return the jersey stored at the current node; otherwise the size of the node's right subtree is k' < k- 1, recurse in the node's down the tree, so it runs in worst-case O(logn) time.left subtree to find its subtree's k"h highest performing player. 35632	Mind 语言 · 中英文混合规范
35634	你实际写 Mind 时，是中英文混合的——这是对的。Mind 不是“纯中文语言”，也不是“纯英文语言”，而是自然语言优先、中英文自由混合。
35636	核心规则只有一条：用你最自然的方式写出算法步骤。你习惯用英文术语（如 array、max、cache）就用英文，习惯用中文描述就用中文。插件只做两件事：
35638	1. 识别出“动词”和“名词”
35639	2. 分别标成蓝色和绿色
35641	和语言种类无关。
35643	---
35645	一、混合示例（你的真实写法）
35647	```mind
35648	initialize max as array[0]
35649	遍历 array 中每个 element
35650	if element > max
35651	update max to element
35652	return max
35653	```
35655	词 角色 颜色
35656	initialize、遍历、if、update、return 动词 🔵 蓝色
35657	max、array、element 名词 🟢 绿色
35659	你不需要翻译 initialize 成“初始化”，也不需要把 array 写成“数组”。Mind 不规定语言。
35661	---
35663	二、自然语言 + 英文术语混合
35665	```mind
35666	计算 the sum of array
35667	if sum > threshold
35668	打印 result
35669	```
35671	词 角色 颜色
35672	计算、if、打印 动词 🔵 蓝色
35673	sum、array、threshold、result 名词 🟢 绿色
35675	---
35677	三、Mind 不做的
35679	不做的事 理由
35680	强制纯英文或纯中文 不限制，你用最自然的写法
35681	要求统一术语 array 和 数组 都可以，AI 只看语义角色
35682	翻译你的词 保留原样，只判断它是“动作”还是“对象”
35684	---
35686	四、一句话总结
35688	Mind 不规定你用英文还是中文。你写 initialize max 或 初始化 最大值 都行。插件只做两件事：认出动词（蓝色）、认出名词（绿色）。
35690	方舟继续。你可以直接用你习惯的中英混合写法写 .mind 文件，不需要学习任何新规则。
35692	记住这种代码规则
35694	---

36062	Heap Insert
36063	· Append new item x to end of array in O(1) amortized, making it next leaf i in reading order ·max_heapify_up(i): swap with parent until Max-Heap Property
36064	-Check whether Q[parent(i)]≥Q[i] (part of Max-Heap Property at parent(i))
36065	- If not, swap items Q[i] and Q[parent(i)], and recursively max_heapify_up(parent(i))· Correctness:
36066	- Max-Heap Property guarantees all nodes > descendants, except Q[i] might be > some of its ancestors (unless i is the root, so we're done)
36067	- If swap necessary, same guarantee is true with Q[parent(i)] instead of Q[i]
36068	· Running time: height of tree, so O(log n)!

46126	Recitation 9
46127	Graph Representations
46128	There are many ways to represent a graph in code. The most common way is to store a Set data structure Adj mapping each vertex u to another data structure Adj(u) storing the adjacencies of v, i.e., the set of vertices that are accessible from v via a single outgoing edge. This inner data structure is called an adjacency list. Note that we don't store the edge pairs explicitly; we store only the out-going neighbor vertices for each vertex. When vertices are uniquely labeled from 0to|VI- 1, it is common to store the top-level Set Adj within a direct access array of length |VI.where array slot i points to the adjacency list of the vertex labeled i. Otherwise, if the vertices are not labeled in this way, it is also common to use a hash table to map each u E V to Adj(u).Then, it is common to store each adjacency list Adj(u) as a simple unordered array of the outgoing adjacencies. For example, the following are adjacency list representations of G1 and G2, using a direct access array for the top-level Set and an array for each adjacency list.
46129	A2=[[1,4,3],
46130	[0],
46131	[3],
46132	[0,2],
46133	[0]]
46134	Using an array for an adjacency list is a perfectly good data structures if all you need to do is loop over the edges incident to a vertex (which will be the case for all algorithms we will discuss in this class, so will be our default implementation). Each edge appears in any adjacency list at most twice, so the size of an adjacency list representation implemented using arrays is 0(|V| + |E|).A drawback of this representation is that determining whether your graph contains a given edge (u, v) might require Ω2(|V|) time to step through the array representing the adjacency list of u or v.We can overcome this obstacle by storing adjacency lists using hash tables instead of regular un-sorted arrays, which will support edge checking in expected O(1) time, still using only 0(|V|+|E|)space. However, we won't need this operation for our algorithms, so we will assume the simpler unsorted-array-based adjacency list representation. Below are representations of G1 and G2 that use a hash table for both the outer Adj Set and the inner adjacency lists Adj(u), using Python dictionaries:

46300	广度优先搜索
46301	给定一个图，一个常见的查询任务是找到从被查询的顶点出发，通过路径可达的顶点集合。从s开始进行广度优先搜索（BFS）可发现s的层级集合：层级L即为从s通过长度为i的最短路径可达的顶点集合（无法通过长度更短的路径到达）。广度优先搜索以i=0为起点，按递增顺序发现层级，其中Lo=(s)，因为从s通过长度为i=0的路径唯一可达的顶点就是s本身。随后，任何从s通过长度为i+1的最短路径可达的顶点都必须有一条入度边来自其从s的最短路径长度为i的顶点，因此它包含在层级L中。因此，为了计算层级Li+1，需纳入所有与 Ls 中某个尚未被指定层级的顶点之间存在入边关系的顶点。通过从前一层级开始计算每一层级，便可依照这些顶点与起始点s之间的最短路径长度来逐步探索不断增长的顶点范围。

47252	Exercise: Given an unweighted graph G = (V, E), find a shortest path from s to t having an odd number of edges.
47253	lution: Construct anew graph G=(V', E'). For every vertex u in V, construct two vertices uE and uo in V': these represent reaching the vertex u through an even and odd number of edges,respectively. For every edge (u, v) in E, construct the edges (uE,vo) and (uo,vE) in E'. Run breadth-first search on G' from sE to find the shortest path from se to to. Because G' is bipartite between even and odd vertices, even paths from sE will always end at even vertices, and odd paths will end at odd vertices, so finding a shortest path from sE to to will represent a path of odd length in the original graph. Because G' has 2|V| vertices and 2|E| edges, constructing G' and running breadth-first search from sE each take O(|V| +|E|) time.

47763	---
47765	#### 审查结果
47767	##### 1. 插入排序 — ✅ 正确，无修改
47769	O(nk) 是 k-proximate 的紧界，O(n²) 是常规最坏情形，原地+稳定都对。
47771	##### 2. 选择排序 — ✅ 正确
47773	交换次数精确为 n-1 次（每次一轮只交换一次），确实是所有比较排序中交换次数最少的。不稳定也对——例：`[2₁, 2₂, 1]` → `[1, 2₂, 2₁]`。
47775	##### 3. 归并排序 — ✅ 正确
47777	唯一可补充的是：理论上存在 O(1) 额外空间的归并排序变体（in-place merge sort），但实际常数极差且几乎不用于教学，所以"非原地"作为课程级别总结是正确的。
47779	##### 4. AVL 排序 — ⚠️ 有一处需要加注
47781	| 说法 | 判定 |
47782	|------|------|
47783	| O(n log n) 构建 | ✅ |
47784	| 支持 O(log n) 动态操作 | ✅ |
47785	| 非原地（存指针/平衡信息） | ✅ |
47786	| **稳定排序** | ⚠️ 有条件 |
47788	**问题：标准 AVL 树不允许重复键。** 要稳，需要处理等键策略：
47789	- 用序列 AVL（以 `(key, sequence_index)` 为隐式复合键），则稳定
47790	- 用普通 AVL + 相同键插右子树 + 中序遍历时按插入顺序输出，也可稳
47792	这和你的 SCLR 方案中"处理相同出价"是同一个问题。建议在表格中加一句 **"稳定（需处理等键策略）"** 而不是不加限定地标"稳定"。
47794	##### 5. 堆排序 — ✅ 正确
47796	"在比较排序中，同时满足原地 + 最坏 O(n log n) 的唯一选择" — 在教学语境下是对的。
47798	严格来说存在 smoothsort（Dijkstra, 1981）和几种理论变体，但它们不在任何标准算法课程的讨论范围。所以这个"唯一"在考试中是正确的论述。
47800	##### 6. 计数排序 — ✅ 正确
47802	补一个细节：O(n + u)，当 u = O(n) 时才是 O(n)。你的描述中"u = O(n)"已经明确了这个前提，没问题。稳定性取决于实现——标准的带累积频率的版本（右向左填充输出数组）是稳定的，这也是课程中教的版本。✅
47804	##### 7. 基数排序 — ✅ 正确
47806	补一个细节：O(d × (n + b))，其中 d 是位数，b 是基数。当 d 为常数、b = O(n) 时退化为 O(n)。你用 u = O(n^c) 来表达这层意思（选基数 ≈ n，位数 = c），逻辑是对的。
47808	---
47810	#### 总结表格审查
47812	| 约束 | 你的推荐 | 判定 |
47813	|------|---------|------|
47814	| 需要稳定排序 | 归并/AVL | ✅（AVL 加注等键处理） |
47815	| 原地 + O(n log n) | 堆排序 | ✅ |
47816	| 数据基本有序 | 插入排序 | ✅ |
47817	| 写入成本极高 | 选择排序 | ✅ |
47818	| 需要动态操作 | AVL 排序 | ✅ |
47819	| 整数，范围小 | 计数排序 | ✅ |
47820	| 整数，范围大但位数固定 | 基数排序 | ✅ |

47824	#### 最终修正版（直接可用）
47826	> **排序算法核心特性总表**
47827	>
47828	> | 算法 | 擅长 | 缺少 | 原地 | 稳定 |
47829	> |------|------|------|------|------|
47830	> | **插入排序** | k-近似有序数组：O(nk)，数据基本有序时实际最快之一 | 平均/最坏 O(n²)，大规模乱序效率低 | ✅ | ✅ |
47831	> | **选择排序** | 写入/交换成本极高时：仅需 O(n) 次交换 | 恒为 O(n²)，无视数据有序程度 | ✅ | ❌ |
47832	> | **归并排序** | 最坏情况保证 O(n log n)，比较排序最优渐近界 | 非原地，需 O(n) 辅助空间 | ❌ | ✅ |
47833	> | **AVL 排序** | 排序后仍需频繁动态操作：O(n log n) 建树 + O(log n) 增删查 | 非原地（指针/平衡信息），实现复杂 | ❌ | ✅¹ |
47834	> | **堆排序** | 唯一同时满足原地 + 最坏 O(n log n) 的比较排序 | 不稳定，常数因子通常大于快排 | ✅ | ❌ |
47835	> | **计数排序** | 整数且范围 u = O(n)：达到 O(n) 线性时间 | 仅限整数；u 很大时时空爆炸 | ❌ | ✅ |
47836	> | **基数排序** | 整数且位数固定：O(n)，尤其 u = O(n^c) 时高效 | 依赖数字表示，浮点数需特殊编码 | ❌ | ✅² |
47837	>
47838	> ¹ 需处理等键策略（序列 AVL 或等键子树约定），否则不保证稳定
47839	> ² 依赖于排序子程序为稳定排序（如计数排序）
47840	>
47841	> ---
47842	>
47843	> **考试速查：按约束选择算法**
47844	>
47845	> | 题目约束 | 最佳选择 | 原因 |
47846	> |---------|---------|------|
47847	> | 需要稳定排序 | 归并排序 | 基于比较、稳定、保证 O(n log n) |
47848	> | 原地 + O(n log n) | 堆排序 | 比较排序中唯一同时满足两者的选项 |
47849	> | 数据 k-近似有序 | 插入排序 | O(nk)，k 小时远优于 O(n log n) |
47850	> | 写入/交换成本极高 | 选择排序 | 仅 O(n) 次交换，所有比较排序中最少 |
47851	> | 排序后需要动态操作 | AVL 排序 | 建树后支持 O(log n) 的插入/删除/查找 |
47852	> | 整数，范围 u = O(n) | 计数排序 | O(n) 线性时间，突破比较下界 |
47853	> | 整数，范围大但位数固定 | 基数排序 | 用稳定子排序逐位处理，O(n) |
47855	---

54255	· How to find a topological order?
54256	· A Finishing Order is the order in which a Full-DFS finishes visiting each verte ·Claim: If G = (V, E) is a DAG, the reverse of a finishing order is a topological · Proof: Need to prove, for every edge (u, u) E E that u is ordered before v,i.e., the visit to v finishes before visiting u. Two cases:
54257	- If u visited before v:
54258	* Before visit to u finishes, will visit u (via (u, v) or otherwise)* Thus the visit to v finishes before visiting u
54259	- If v visited before u:
54260	* u can't be reached from v since graph is acyclic * Thus the visit to v finishes before visiting u
54262	这个证明的意义是什么

55194	逐条审查。
55196	---
55198	#### 审查结果
55200	##### 排序数组 — ⚠️ 有一处错误
55202	| 说法 | 判定 |
55203	|------|------|
55204	| find O(log n) | ✅ |
55205	| find_min O(1) | ✅ 首元素 |
55206	| find_max O(1) | ✅ 尾元素 |
55207	| **find_next O(1)** | ❌ **应为 O(log n)** |
55208	| insert/delete O(n) | ✅ |
55210	**问题**：`find_next(k)` 在标准 Set 接口中意为"找比 k 大的最小 key"。排序数组需要先二分查找定位 k（O(log n)），再取下一元素（O(1)）。**总时间 O(log n)，不是 O(1)。**
55212	如果你用"已有元素引用，找下一个"的迭代器语义，那确实 O(1)，但这不是 Set ADT 的标准用法——标准用法传的是 key，不是引用。
55214	##### 直接访问数组 — ✅ 正确
55216	所有操作 O(1) worst-case，前提是非负整数 key 且 u = O(n)。无任何修正。
55218	##### 哈希表 — ✅ 正确
55220	期望 O(1)、有序操作 O(n)、最坏可退化。都正确。
55222	##### 集合 AVL 树 — ✅ 正确
55224	所有操作 O(log n) worst-case、支持有序操作、非原地、建树 O(n log n)。都正确。
55226	---
55228	#### 选择指南审查
55230	| 场景 | 你的推荐 | 判定 |
55231	|------|---------|------|
55232	| key ∈ [0, n-1] | 直接访问数组 | ✅ |
55233	| 字符串/任意类型，需期望 O(1) | 哈希表 | ✅ |
55234	| 需最坏 O(log n) 保证 | AVL | ✅ |
55235	| 需有序操作 | AVL 或排序数组 | ✅ |
55236	| 动态插入删除 + 有序操作 | AVL | ✅ |
55237	| 静态数据，建一次，频繁查 | 排序数组 | ✅ |
55239	全部正确。静态场景选排序数组的理由：和 AVL 同是 O(n log n) 建、O(log n) 查，但无指针开销、缓存友好、空间更紧。
55241	---
55243	#### 最终修正版
55245	> **集合数据结构核心特性总表**
55246	>
55247	> | 数据结构 | 核心操作 | 有序操作 | 擅长 | 缺少 |
55248	> |---------|---------|---------|------|------|
55249	> | **排序数组** | find O(log n)；insert/delete O(n) | find_min/max O(1)；find_next/prev O(log n) | 二分查找快；最值 O(1)；静态数据无额外开销 | 插入删除需移动元素 O(n) |
55250	> | **直接访问数组** | 全部 O(1) worst-case | 不支持（key 必须是下标，无序概念） | 无哈希冲突、无指针、无摊销，最快的字典 | 仅限非负整数 key；需 u = O(n)，否则空间爆炸 |
55251	> | **哈希表** | find/insert/delete 期望 O(1) | O(n)，需全表扫描 | 支持任意可哈希类型；通用性最强 | 有序操作极慢；最坏可退化至 O(n) |
55252	> | **集合 AVL 树** | 全部 O(log n) worst-case | 全部 O(log n) | 最坏硬保证；支持有序操作；可增广 | 非原地（指针/平衡信息）；实现复杂 |
55253	>
55254	> **有序操作说明**：find_min（最小值）、find_max（最大值）、find_prev(k)（前驱，比 k 小的最大 key）、find_next(k)（后继，比 k 大的最小 key）。排序数组的 `find_next` 需要先二分定位 key（O(log n)），再取下一元素——所以是 O(log n)，不是 O(1)。
55256	---
55258	> **术语速查**
55259	>
55260	> | 术语 | 含义 |
55261	> |------|------|
55262	> | O(1) | 常数时间，不随数据量增长 |
55263	> | O(log n) | 对数时间，n 翻倍仅增常数步 |
55264	> | O(n) | 线性时间，与数据量成正比 |
55265	> | 期望 O(1) | 平均 O(1)，最坏可能退化（如哈希冲突） |
55266	> | 最坏 O(log n) | 无论输入如何，保证 ≤ O(log n)（AVL 的硬保证） |
55267	> | 摊销 | 偶尔单次操作慢（如哈希扩容），但均摊到每次是 O(1) |
55269	---
55271	> **考试速查：按场景选择**
55272	>
55273	> | 场景 | 选择 | 原因 |
55274	> |------|------|------|
55275	> | key 是 0 到 n-1 的整数 | 直接访问数组 | O(1) 最坏，无任何额外开销，字典实现的天花板 |
55276	> | key 是字符串/任意类型，需 O(1) 期望 | 哈希表 | 通用性最强，实际性能极好 |
55277	> | 需要 O(log n) 最坏保证，不允许退化 | 集合 AVL 树 | 哈希表可能退化，AVL 是硬保证 |
55278	> | 需要有序操作（前驱/后继） | AVL 树（动态）或排序数组（静态） | 两者都支持；动态场景必选 AVL |
55279	> | 需动态插入/删除 + 有序操作 | 集合 AVL 树 | 排序数组插入删除 O(n)，AVL 是 O(log n) |
55280	> | 静态数据，建一次，频繁查询 | 排序数组 | O(n log n) 建好后 O(log n) 查，无指针开销，缓存友好 |
55282	---
55284	#### 修改总结
55286	| 位置 | 问题 | 修正 |
55287	|------|------|------|
55288	| 排序数组 find_next | 标为 O(1) | 改为 O(log n)，并加注说明原因 |
55289	| 直接访问数组 | 未说明"无有序操作"概念 | 补充：key 即下标，不存在序的概念 |
55290	| 选择指南 | 全部正确 | 无修改 |
55292	只此一处实质性错误，其余全部正确。结构清晰、维度完整，直接可用。

55549	---
55551	#### 一、序列接口 — 全部正确 ✅
55553	| 数据结构 | 说法 | 判定 |
55554	|---------|------|------|
55555	| 数组 | get_at/set_at O(1)；insert_at/delete_at O(n) | ✅ |
55556	| 链表 | insert_first/delete_first O(1)；get_at/set_at O(n) | ✅ |
55557	| 动态数组 | 同数组 + insert_last/delete_last 摊销 O(1) | ✅ |
55558	| 序列 AVL 树 | 全部 O(log n)；子树增广 size；非原地 | ✅ |
55560	序列 AVL 树的"增广 size 支持按索引查找"是关键——它把序列问题转化成了 order statistics 问题，这正是你 SCLR 方案中用 `subtree_count` 的思路。
55562	---
55564	#### 二、集合接口 — 全部正确 ✅
55566	| 数据结构 | 说法 | 判定 |
55567	|---------|------|------|
55568	| 排序数组 | find O(log n)；min/max O(1)；insert/delete O(n)；find_next/prev O(log n) | ✅ 已修正 |
55569	| 直接访问数组 | 全部 O(1)；仅限非负整数；需 u = O(n) | ✅ |
55570	| 哈希表 | find/insert/delete 期望 O(1)；有序操作 O(n)；最坏退化 | ✅ |
55571	| 集合 AVL 树 | 全部 O(log n) worst-case；支持有序；可增广；非原地 | ✅ |
55573	---
55575	#### 三、考试速查表 — ⚠️ 有两处需补充
55577	| 需求 | 你的推荐 | 判定 |
55578	|------|---------|------|
55579	| 按索引 get_at(i) 快 | 数组/动态数组 | ✅ |
55580	| 按索引 + 中间插入删除 | 序列 AVL 树 | ✅ |
55581	| 只在头部/尾部增删 | 动态数组（尾）或链表（头） | ⚠️ |
55582	| 按键 find(k) 快 | 哈希表 或 AVL | ✅ |
55583	| 键是 0~n-1 整数 | 直接访问数组 | ✅ |
55584	| 需要有序操作 | AVL（动态）或排序数组（静态） | ⚠️ |
55586	##### 问题 1：头部/尾部增删
55588	链表**尾部** `insert_last`/`delete_last` 是 O(n)（需遍历到末尾），除非是双向链表 + 维护尾指针，或循环链表。这里只写了"链表（头）"，建议明确限制为头部。同时动态数组 `insert_last` 的"摊销"二字比"头"更有意义——建议一行保持一致精度。
55590	##### 问题 2：需要有序操作
55592	只提了 AVL 和排序数组，但**直接访问数组**如果 key 本身就是位置（即排序后的序等同于数组下标），有序操作也是 O(1)。不过这是 trivial case——你的"键是 0~n-1 整数"已经单独成行，这里不必赘述。✅ 不改也行。
55594	---
55596	#### 最终修正版
55598	> **一、序列接口 (Sequence)：按位置操作**
55599	>
55600	> 操作语义：`get_at(i)` 取第 i 个元素，`set_at(i, x)` 改第 i 个元素，`insert_at(i, x)` 在第 i 位插入，`delete_at(i)` 删除第 i 个元素，以及首尾变体 `insert_first`/`delete_first`、`insert_last`/`delete_last`。顺序由外部显式指定。
55601	>
55602	> | 数据结构 | 擅长 | 缺少 |
55603	> |---------|------|------|
55604	> | **数组** | get_at / set_at O(1)，按索引直接访问 | insert_at / delete_at O(n)，需移动后续所有元素 |
55605	> | **链表** | insert_first / delete_first O(1)，仅修改指针即可 | get_at / set_at O(n)，无法随机访问，必须从头遍历 |
55606	> | **动态数组** | 同数组；此外 insert_last / delete_last 摊销 O(1) | 中间 insert_at / delete_at 仍为 O(n) |
55607	> | **序列 AVL 树** | 全部操作 O(log n) worst-case；通过子树增广 size 将索引映射为 order statistics | 非原地（指针/平衡信息）；实现远比其他三种复杂 |
55608	>
55609	> ---
55610	>
55611	> **二、集合接口 (Set)：按键值操作**
55612	>
55613	> 操作语义：`find(k)` 查找，`insert(x)` 插入，`delete(k)` 删除；有序操作 `find_min`/`find_max`（最值）、`find_prev(k)`（前驱）/`find_next(k)`（后继）。顺序由 key 的内在序决定。
55614	>
55615	> | 数据结构 | 擅长 | 缺少 |
55616	> |---------|------|------|
55617	> | **排序数组** | find O(log n) 二分；find_min / find_max O(1) | insert / delete O(n)，需移动元素；find_prev / find_next O(log n) |
55618	> | **直接访问数组** | 全部操作 O(1) worst-case，无哈希冲突，无摊销，最快的字典实现 | 仅限非负整数 key；需 key 范围 u = O(n)，否则空间爆炸 |
55619	> | **哈希表** | find / insert / delete 期望 O(1)；支持任意可哈希类型，通用性最强 | 有序操作 O(n)，需全表扫描；最坏情况可能退化至 O(n)（哈希碰撞） |
55620	> | **集合 AVL 树** | 全部 O(log n) worst-case 硬保证；支持全部有序操作；节点可增广 | 非原地（每个节点存指针和平衡信息）；建树 O(n log n) |
55621	>
55622	> 注：排序数组的 `find_prev`/`find_next` 不是 O(1)——需先二分定位 key（O(log n)），再取相邻元素。只有 `find_min`/`find_max` 是 O(1)（直接取首/尾元素）。
55623	>
55624	> ---
55625	>
55626	> **三、考试速查：按需求选择**
55627	>
55628	> | 需求 | 选什么 | 原因 |
55629	> |------|--------|------|
55630	> | 按索引 get_at(i) 快 | 数组 / 动态数组 | O(1) 随机访问 |
55631	> | 按索引 + 还需要中间插入删除 | 序列 AVL 树 | 全部 O(log n)，数组做不到 |
55632	> | 只在头部增删 | 链表 | O(1)，仅修改指针 |
55633	> | 只在尾部增删 | 动态数组 | insert_last / delete_last 摊销 O(1) |
55634	> | 按键 find(k) 快 | 哈希表（期望 O(1)）或集合 AVL（最坏 O(log n)） | 前者快但有退化风险，后者硬保证 |
55635	> | 键是 0 到 n-1 的整数 | 直接访问数组 | O(1) worst-case，无任何额外开销 |
55636	> | 需要有序操作（前驱/后继） | 集合 AVL（动态）；排序数组（静态，建后不改） | 两者都支持；动态场景必选 AVL |
55638	---
55640	#### 修改总结
55642	| 位置 | 问题 | 修正 |
55643	|------|------|------|
55644	| 原"只在头部/尾部增删" | 链表尾部增删是 O(n)，合在一起有歧义 | 拆成两行：头→链表 O(1)，尾→动态数组摊销 O(1) |
55645	| 原"需要有序操作" | 只提了两种，缺静态/动态区分 | 补全静态（排序数组）和动态（AVL）的场景说明 |
55647	两张表的分离决策是对的——序列和集合是两种不同的 ADT，接口不同，没有直接可比性。分开分析避免了概念混淆，也正好对应了 6.042J 中 ADT vs 数据结构的经典区分。整个输出结构清晰、无实质性错误，可以直接作为复习卡片使用。💪

Given the n short-circuiting pairs of friends, describe an O(n)-time algorithm to determine whether Romie-0 and Julie-8 can invite all of their friends to two peaceful parties, without anyone short-circuiting.
57018	Solution: Construct a graph G where each vertex is a friend who might short-circuit, with an undirected edge between a pair of friends if they make each other short-circuit. Note that we can ignore any friend not participating in short-circuiting because they have no restrictions on which party they can attend. We can assign the friends to two peaceful parties if and only if there is a coloring of the vertices of G with two colors such that no edge connects vertices of the same color, i.e., the graph must be bipartite. To determine whether the graph is bipartite, we will either find a valid two-coloring, or find an odd-length cycle in the graph (if there is an odd-length cycle in the graph, there certainly cannot be a valid two-coloring of the cycle or the graph).
57019	To find a possible two-coloring of G, our approach will be to find a spanning forest F of G, two-color it,and then check to see whether any edge in G violates the coloring. If there is an edge {u, v} such that both vertices have the same color, then the path between u and v in F has even length (since it has a valid two-coloring), so adding {u, v} would be an odd-length cycle.
57020	Running either Full-BFS or Full-DFS on G can construct a spanning forest F. We choose to run Full-BFS,marking each vertex with its shortest path distance to the arbitrarily chosen source within its connected component. To two-color F, assign one color to all vertices with even distance to their source, and secondcolor to all vertices with odd distance to their source (since shortest paths alternate distance parity along the path). Lastly, check whether every edge in the graph has endpoints assigned opposite colors. If not, return parties is possible.that two parties is impossible. Otherwise the coloring confirms the graph is bipartite, so return that two
57021	G has size O(n) since it has n edges and at most 2n vertices, and can be constructed in as much time.perform a constant-time check. So this algorithm runs in O(n) time.Running Full-BFS on G takes time O(n) (linear in the size of G), and then for each of the n edges we

57479	This graph has the property that a path between any two vertices corresponds to a route on the map that does not trample crops. It remains how to find the shortest such route between any vertex adjacent to a 'euphris' square to a vertex adjacent to a 'tigrates' square. For each 'euphris' square Mr][c.of the route), and mark 'tigrates' vertices similarly.mark vertices {(r,c),(r+1,c),(r,c+1),(r+1,c+1)}as'euphris' vertices (possible starting intersection
57480	We could solve SSSP from each ' euphris' vertex using BFS, but that would take too much time (poten-tially Ω2(n2) 'euphris' vertices, with each BFS taking Ω(n2) time.) So instead, add a supernode s to G with an undirected edge from s to each 'euphris' vertex in G, to construct graph G'. Then any possible trade route will correspond to a path from s to a 'tigrates' vertex in G' (without the first edge), and the trade route will be the shortest among them. So run BFS from s to every 'tigrates' vertex, and return the shortest path to the closest one by traversing parent pointers back to the source.
57481	Graph G'has (n+1)2+1 vertices and O(n2) + O(n2) edges, so can be constructed in O(n2) time, and running BFS once from s also takes O(n2) time, so this algorithm runs in O(n2) time in total.

64250	---
64377	#### 公式问题诊断
64379	你的质疑完全正确。我的公式有一个**遗漏的前置条件**。
64381	---
64383	##### 公式回顾
64385	```
64386	N_r^→ = #{(c_1', …, c_k') | L_i < c_i' ≤ c_i,  c_1' < … < c_k'}
64387	```
64389	其中 L_i 是滑块 i 左侧最近的障碍物列号。
64391	---
64393	##### 它漏了什么？
64395	**反例：** n = 6, 无障碍物, B 中滑块位于 c₁ = 2, c₂ = 4。
64397	按我的公式：
64398	- L₁ = L₂ = -1
64399	- c₁' ∈ {0, 1, 2}
64400	- c₂' ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}
64401	- c₁' < c₂' → 共 9 个
64403	但取 B' = (c₁'=0, c₂'=1)，模拟 → 倾斜：
64405	```
64406	滑块2 从1出发 → 无障碍阻挡 → 滑到边缘 n-1=5
64407	滑块1 从0出发 → 被滑块2阻挡 → 停在4
64408	最终配置: (4, 5) ≠ (2, 4) ✗
64409	```
64411	**B 根本无法通过 → 倾斜达到！** 公式却返回了 9。
64413	---
64415	##### 缺失的前置条件：B 必须「可达」
64417	对于 → 倾斜，滑块在 B 中的最终位置必须有**阻挡物**才能停住：
64419	| 滑块 i 停在 c_i 的条件 | 说明 |
64420	|------------------------|------|
64421	| cᵢ = n-1 | 棋盘右边缘 |
64422	| cᵢ+1 处有障碍物 | 被障碍物阻挡 |
64423	| cᵢ+1 处有另一个滑块（即 c_{i+1} = cᵢ+1） | 被下一个滑块阻挡 |
64425	**若某一行的滑块不满足上述条件，则 P_→ = 0（整行无前驱）。**
64427	对于上面的反例：c₂=4，既不是边缘(n-1=5)，右边(5)又无障碍物，也没有滑块紧跟→ B 在该行不可达。
64429	---
64431	##### 对于可达的 B，公式是否正确？
64433	**正确。** 验证如下：
64435	**例：** n=8, B: c₁=4, c₂=5, c₃=6, 障碍物在列 7。
64437	```
64438	可达性检查：
64439	c₃=6 → 障碍物在7 ✓
64440	c₂=5 → 相邻于c₃ (5+1=6) ✓
64441	c₁=4 → 相邻于c₂ (4+1=5) ✓
64442	```
64444	取 B' = (c₁'=0, c₂'=1, c₃'=2)：
64446	```
64447	滑块3 从2出发 → 障碍物在7 → 停在6 ✓
64448	滑块2 从1出发 → 被滑块3阻挡 → 停在5 ✓
64449	滑块1 从0出发 → 被滑块2阻挡 → 停在4 ✓
64450	最终: (4, 5, 6) = B ✓
64451	```
64453	此时公式 `0 < c₁' ≤ 4, 0 < c₂' ≤ 5, 0 < c₃' ≤ 6, 保序` 枚举出的每一个 (c₁', c₂', c₃') 都是有效前驱。
64455	**为什么？** 因为一旦 B 可达，滑块 i 若被滑块 i+1 阻挡，则滑块 i+1 **必定停在 c_i+1**。无论滑块 i+1 是从哪里出发的（只要它在 c_{i+1}' 且 L_{i+1} < c_{i+1}' ≤ c_{i+1}），它都会滑到 c_{i+1} 停住，滑块 i 也就会停在 c_i。公式中的 `c_i' < c_{i+1}'` 保证了滑块不会互相穿越，而 `c_i' > L_i` 保证路径上无障碍物——两者合起来恰好刻画了"滑块 i 追尾滑块 i+1 并停在其后一格"的全部语义。
64457	---
64459	##### 修正后的完整公式
64461	对每个方向 d，先检查 B 在该方向上是否可达，不可达则 P_d = 0；可达则用分解公式：
64463	\[
64464	\boxed{
64465	P_d =
64466	\begin{cases}
64467	\displaystyle\prod_{\text{行 }r} N_{r,d} & d \in \{\leftarrow, \rightarrow\} \\[18pt]
64468	\displaystyle\prod_{\text{列 }c} N_{c,d} & d \in \{\uparrow, \downarrow\}
64469	\end{cases}
64470	}
64471	\]
64473	其中单行/列公式不变（你原文那个）。关键是**先判断可达性**，否则公式会对不可达的 B 给出假阳性结果。
64475	---
64477	##### 一句话总结
64479	你的公式**逻辑是对的**，但它隐含了"B 是某次倾斜的可能结果"这一前提。把这个前置条件显式写出后，公式就能正确计算任意 B 在任意方向上的前驱数量。

70969	Problem 5-1. Graph Radius
70970	In any undirected graph G=(V,E), the eccentricity e(u) of a vertex u E V is the shortest distance to its farthest vertex v,i.e., e(u)=max{8(u,v)|vE V).Theradius R(G) of an undirected graph G=(V, E)is the smallest eccentricity of any vertex, i.e., R(G)=min(e(u)|uEV).
70971	(a) Given connected undirected graph G, describe an O(V]|E])-time algorithm to determine the radius of G.
70972	(b) Given connected undirected graph G,describe an O(]E])-time algorithm to determine an upper bound R' on the radius of G, such that R(G) ≤ R ≤ 2R(G).
70973	Problem 5-2. Internet Investigation
70974	MIT has heard complaints regarding the speed of their WiFi network. The network consists of r routers,some of which are marked as entry points which are connected to the rest of the internet. Some pairs of routers are directly connected to each other via bidirectional wires. Each wire wy between two routers has a known length & measured in a positive integer number of feet. The lateney of a router in the network is proportional to the minimum feet of wire a signal from the router must pass through to reach an entry point.Assume the latency of every router is finite and there is at most 100r feet of wire in the entire network.Given a schematic of the network depicting all routers and the lengths of all wires, describe an O(r)-time algorithm to determine the sum total latency, summed over all routers in the network.
70975	Problem 5-3.Quadwizard Quest
70976	Wizard Potry Harter and her three wizard friends have been tasked with searching every room of a Labyrinth for magical artifacts. The Labyrinth consists of n rooms, where each room has at most four doors leading to other rooms. Assume all doors begin closed and every room in the Labyrinth is reachable from a specified entry room by traversing doors between rooms. Some doors are protected by evil enchantments that must be disenchanted before they can be opened; but all other doors may be opened freely. 72585	---
72625	模式 1: Hash + AVL（快查 + 有序）
72627	场景：需要按 key 快速查对象，还需要按某种顺序遍历。
72629	结构:
72631	hash_table: key → AVL_node_ptr (O(1) find)
72633	avl_tree: ordered by <criteria> (O(log n) order ops)
72635	插入(x):
72637	node = avl.insert(x)
72639	hash_table[x.key] = node # O(log n)
72641	查找(key):
72643	node = hash_table[key] # O(1) expected
72645	return node.value
72647	按序遍历():
72649	avl.inorder() # O(n)
72651	删除(key):
72653	node = hash_table[key] # O(1) expected
72655	avl.delete(node) # O(log n)
72657	hash_table.remove(key) # O(1) expected
72659	考场信号词： "maintain a set of items, support lookup by ID, and report in sorted order"
72661	模式 2: Heap + Hash（PQ + 查找）
72663	场景：需要按优先级取极值，但也要按 key 查找/更新。
72665	结构:
72667	heap: array[0..n-1] (priority order)
72669	hash_table: key → heap_index (O(1) find)
72671	insert(key, priority):
72673	i = heap.push(key, priority)
72675	hash_table[key] = i
72677	extract_max():
72679	key = heap.pop_max()
72681	hash_table.remove(key)
72683	return key
72685	update_priority(key, new_priority):
72687	i = hash_table[key] # O(1)
72689	heap.change_priority_at(i, new_priority) # O(log n)
72691	精要：哈希表直接存堆索引， change_priority 时在堆中上浮/下沉。
72693	模式 3: AVL ⼦树增强（⾃定义聚合）
72695	场景：需要在⼆叉树中快速查询⼦树聚合信息（求和、最值、⼤⼩等）。AVL 增强的通用配方:
72697	1. 选择一个属性 P(node)
72699	2. 要求: P(node) 能只用 P(node.left) 和 P(node.right) 在 O(1) 算出
72701	3. 旋转维护: 旋转后重新计算受影响节点的 P
72703	4. 插入/删除后沿路径向上更新 P
72705	例: subtree_size
72707	P(node) = P(node.left) + P(node.right) + 1
72709	旋转后: 只需重算旋转涉及的两个节点
72711	例: subtree_max
72713	P(node) = max(node.val, P(node.left), P(node.right))
72715	例: max_consecutive_active (Vapor Invite Q9)
72717	P(node) = (prefix_len, suffix_len, max_len, total_len)
72719	可从左右子节点组合 → O(1) 维护
72721	精要：AVL 增强的唯⼀前提是属性必须能从⼦树向上传播。
72723	模式 4: 多级索引（范围查询 + 批量更新）
72725	场景：按某个维度做范围查询，⼜要在另⼀个维度快速查找。
72727	例 (Methane Menace Q8):
72729	hash_table: site_id → (depth, data) (按 ID 查)
72731	avl_tree: ordered by depth (按 depth 范围查)
72733	avl 节点增强: subtree_size (计数)
72735	report(d1, d2):
72737	→ avl.range_query(d1, d2) # O(log n + k)
72739	add_site(id, depth):
72741	node = avl.insert(depth, id)
72743	hash_table[id] = node
72745	remove_site(id):
72747	node = hash_table[id]
72749	avl.delete(node)
72751	hash_table.remove(id)
72753	精要：每个维度⼀个索引。查哪个维度⾛哪个树。更新同时在两个结构中做。
72757	把这几个模式改为思想而非实现

79420	Bellman-Ford
79421	In lecture, we presented a version of Bellman-Ford' based on graph duplication and DAG Re-laxation that solves SSSPs in O(|V||E]) time and space, and can return a negative-weight cycle reachable on a path from s to v, for any vertex v with 5(s,v)=-oo.
79422	The original Bellman-Ford algorithm is easier to state but is a litle less powerful. It solves SSSPs in the same time using only O(IVI) space, but only detects whether a negative-weight cycle exists (will not return such a negative weight cycle). It is based on the relaxation framework discussed in RII The algorithm is straight-forward: initialize distance estinates, and then relax every edge in the graph in V-1 rounds. The claim is that: if the graph does not contain negative-weightcycles,d(s,v)=5(5,v)forall E Vat terination; otherwise if any edge still relaxable(, still violates the triangle inequality), the graph contains a negative weight cycle. A Python implementation of the Bellman-Ford algorithm is given below.: def bellman_ford(Adj, w, #):
79423	Adj: adjacency list, w: weights, s: start # number greater than sum of all + weights # shortest path estimates d(s, v)initialize parent pointers # initialize source
79424	initialization
79425	infinity = float('inf')
79426	d= [infinity for _ in Adj]
79427	parent = [None for _ in Adj]
79428	disl, parentis] - O, a
79429	& construct shortest paths in rounds
79430	Ve len(Adj)
79431	i number of vertices
79432	fork in range(V-1):
79433	&relax all edges in(V-1) rounds
79434	for u in range(V);

79768	这个负权环检测什么原理
79770	---
79829	你的直觉很敏锐，但这里确实不是循环位置的问题，而是同步更新的逻辑问题。
79831	---
79833	核心：d[v] 和 parent[v] 必须同步更新
79835	parent[v] 记录的是“到达 v 的最短路径上，v 的前驱是谁”。当发现一条更短的路径 d[u] + w(u, v) 时，同时要更新两样东西：
79837	1. d[v]：新的最短距离。
79838	2. parent[v]：新的前驱，即 u。
79840	这两个更新必须在同一个 if 条件下发生，否则 parent[v] 就和 d[v] 不一致了。
79842	---
79844	如果放在 for u 循环外面会怎样？
79846	假设代码写成这样：
79848	```python
79849	for u in range(V):
79850	best_dist = d[v]
79851	best_u = None
79852	for v in Adj[u]:
79853	if d[v] > d[u] + w(u, v):
79854	d[v] = d[u] + w(u, v)
79855	best_u = u    # 暂存 u
79856	parent[v] = best_u    # 错误！移到外面
79857	```
79859	问题：v 可能从多个不同的 u 都能到达。内层 for v 循环结束后，best_u 只保留最后一个尝试松弛的 u，而这个 u 不一定是真正让 d[v] 变小的那个。此外，如果 d[v] 在这一轮没有被任何 u 更新（即原来的 d[v] 已经是最优的），best_u 可能是 None 或者上一个顶点的残余值，parent[v] 会被错误覆盖。
79861	所以，parent[v] = u 必须紧跟在 d[v] 的更新语句后面，放在同一个 if 块里。它不是在“循环 u”时确定的，而是在“发现一条更短路径”时确定的。
79864	你再分析

81318	Lemma 1 At the end of relaxation round i of Bellman-Ford, d(s,D)=6(s,v)for any vertex v that has a shortest path from s to u which traverses at most i edges.Proof.Proof by induction on round i. At the start of the algorithm (at end of round 0), the only vertex with shortest path from & traversing at most 0 edges is vertex s, and Bellman-Ford correctly sets d(s,8)=0=5(s,s). Now suppose the claim is true at the end of round i-1.Let v be a vertex containing a shortest path from s traversing at most i edges. If v has a shortest path from 8traversing at most i-1 edges, d(s,v)=6(s,v) prior to round i, and will continue to hold at the end of round i by the upper-bound property2 Alternatively, d(s,v)≠5(s,v) prior to round i, and let u be the second to last vertex visited along some shortest path from s to v which traverses exactly i edges. Some shortest path from s to u traverses at most i-1 edges, so d(s,u)=6(s,u) prior to round i. Then after the edge from u to v is relaxed during round i, d(s,v)=6(s, v) as desired.□If the graph does not contain negative weight cycles, some shortest path is simple, and contains at most|V|-I edges as it traverses any vertex of the graph at most once.Thus after|V|-1rounds of Bellman-Ford, d(s,v)=6(s, u) for every vertex with a simple shortest path from s to v. However,if after|V|-1rounds of relaxation, some edge (u, v) still violates the triangle inequality (lines 14-17),then there existsa path fromtousing|V| edges which has lower weight than all paths using fewer edges. Such a path cannot e simple, so it must contain a negative weight cycle.This algorithm runs |V| rounds, where each round performs a constant amount of work for each edge in the graph, so Bellman-Ford runs in O(|V||E|) time. Note that lines 10-11 actually take O(|V|+|E|) time to loop over the entire adjacency list structure, even for vertices adjacent to no edge. If the graph contains isolated vertices that are not S, we can just remove them from Adj to ensure that |V|=O(|E|). Note that if edges are processed in a topological sort order with respect to a shortest path tree from s, then Bellman-Ford will correctly compute shortest paths from s after its first round; of course, it is not easy to find such an order. However, for many graphs, significant savings can be obtained by stopping Bellman-Ford after any round for which no edge relaxation is modifying.
81319	Note that this algorithm is different than the one presented in lecture in two important ways:
81320	·The original Bellman-Ford only keeps track of one 'layer' of d(s, v) estimates in each round,while the lecture version keeps track of d(s, v) for k ∈{0,...,[V}, which can be then used to construct negative-weight cycles.
81321	·A distance estimate d(s, v) in round I: of original Bellman-Ford does not necessarily equal dh(s,v), the k-edge distance to vcomputed in the lecture version. This is because the original Bellman-Ford may relax multiple edges along a shortest path to v in a single round, while the lecture version relaxes at most one in each level. In other words, distance estimate d(s,v)in round I: of original Bellman-Ford is never larger than dk(s, t), but it may be much smaller and converge to a solution quicker than the lecture version, so may be faster in practice.'Recall that the Safety Lemma from Recitation 11 ensures that relaxation maintains (,v) ≤ d(s, v) for all v.

89902	Correctness
89903	·Claim: At end of Dijkstra's algorithm, d(s,v) =5(s, v) for all v E V
89904	·Proof:
89905	-If relaxation sets d(s,v) to s(s, v), then d(s, u) = 5(s, v) at the end of the algorithm
89906	*Relaxation can only decrease estimates d(s,v)
89907	*Relaxation is safe, i.e., maintains that each d(s, v) is weight of a path to v (or ∞)-Suffices to show d(s,v)=s(s,v) when vertex v is removed from Q
89908	*Proof by induction on first k vertices removed fromQ
89909	*Base Case (k =1): s is first vertex removed from Q, and d(s, s) =0=5(s,s)* Inductive Step: Assume true for k < k', consider k'th vertex v' removed from Q *Consider some shortest path π from s to v', with w(π)=5(s,v')
89910	*Let (x, y) be the first edge in π where y is not among first k' - 1 (perhaps y =v)*When x was removed from Q, d(s, x) = 5(s, x) by induction, so:
89911	d(s,y)≤5(s,x)+ w(x,y) relaxed edge (x, y) when removed x
89912	=5(s,y)
89913	subpaths of shortest paths are shortest paths
89914	≤ 5(s,v')
89915	non-negative edge weights
89916	≤ d(s,v')
89917	relaxation is safe
89918	≤ d(s,y)
89919	v' is vertex with minimum d(s, v') in Q
89920	*So d(s,v') =5(s,v'), as desired

99989	Dijkstra’s
99991	Algorithm
99993	Dijkstra is possibly the most commonly used weighted shortest paths algorithm; it is asymptoti
99994	-
99996	cally faster than Bellman-Ford, but only applies to graphs containing non-negative edge weights,
99997	which appear often in many applications. The algorithm is fairly intuitive, though its implemen
99998	-
100000	tation can be more complicated than that of other shortest path algorithms. Think of a weighted
100001	graph as a network of pipes, each with non-negative length (weight). Then turn on a water faucet at
100002	a source vertex
100004	s
100005	. Assuming the water flowing from the faucet traverses each pipe at the same rate,
100006	the water will reach each pipe intersection vertex in the order of their shortest distance from the
100007	source. Dijkstra’s algorithm discretizes this continuous process by repeatedly relaxing edges from
100008	a vertex whose minimum weight path estimate is smallest among vertices whose out-going edges
100009	have not yet been relaxed. In order to efficiently find the smallest minimum weight path estimate,
100010	Dijkstra’s algorithm is often presented in terms of a minimum priority queue data structure. Dijk
100011	-
100013	stra’s running time then depends on how efficiently the priority queue can perform its supported
100014	operations. Below is Python code for Dijkstra’s algorithm in terms of priority queue operations.

100248	This algorithm follows the same structure as the general relaxation framework. Lines 2-4 initialize
100249	shortest path weight estimates and parent pointers. Lines 5-7 initialize a priority queue with all
100250	vertices from the graph. Lines 8-12 comprise the main loop. Each time the loop is executed, line
100251	9 removes a vertex from the queue, so the queue will be empty at the end of the loop. The vertex
100252	u
100254	processed in some iteration of the loop is a vertex from the queue whose shortest path weight
100255	estimate is smallest, from among all vertices not yet removed from the queue. Then, lines 10-11
100256	relax the out-going edges from
100258	u
100260	as usual. However, since relaxation may reduce the shortest path
100261	weight estimate
100263	d
100264	(
100265	s,
100267	v
100268	)
100269	, vertex
100271	v
100272	’s key in the queue must be updated (if it still exists in the queue);
100273	line 12 accomplishes this update.
100274	2
100275	Recitation
100277	13
100279	Why does Dijkstra’s algorithm compute shortest paths for a graph with non-negative edge weights?
100280	The key observation is that shortest path weight estimate of vertex
100282	u
100284	equals its actual shortest path
100285	weight
100287	d
100288	(
100289	s,
100291	u
100292	) =
100294	δ
100295	(
100296	s,
100298	u
100299	)
100301	when
100303	u
100305	is removed from the priority queue. Then by the upper-bound
100306	property,
100308	d
100309	(
100310	s,
100312	u
100313	) =
100315	δ
100316	(
100317	s,
100319	u
100320	)
100322	will still hold at termination of the algorithm. A proof of correctness is
100323	described in the lecture notes, and will not be repeated here. Instead, we will focus on analyzing
100324	running time for Dijkstra implemented using different priority queues.

100334	Priority
100336	Queues
100338	An important aspect of Dijkstra’s algorithm is the use of a priority queue.
100340	The priority queue
100341	interface used here differs slightly from our presentation of priority queues earlier in the term.
100342	Here, a priority queue maintains a set of key-value pairs, where vertex
100344	v
100346	is a value and
100348	d
100349	(
100350	s,
100352	v
100353	)
100355	is its
100356	key. Aside from empty initialization, the priority queue supports three operations:

101270	Fibonacci Heaps are not actually used very often in practice as it is more complex to implement,
101271	and results in larger constant factor overhead than the other two implementations described above.
101272	When the number of edges in the graph is known to be at most linear (e.g., planar or bounded
101273	degree graphs) or at least quadratic (e.g. complete graphs) in the number of vertices, then using a
101274	binary heap or dictionary respectively will perform as well asymptotically as a Fibonacci Heap.

101564	Dijkstra’s Algorithm
101565	Dijkstra is possibly the most commonly used weighted shortest paths algorithm; it is asymptoti￾cally faster than Bellman-Ford, but only applies to graphs containing non-negative edge weights,
101566	which appear often in many applications. The algorithm is fairly intuitive, though its implemen￾tation can be more complicated than that of other shortest path algorithms. Think of a weighted
101567	graph as a network of pipes, each with non-negative length (weight). Then turn on a water faucet at
101568	a source vertex s. Assuming the water flowing from the faucet traverses each pipe at the same rate,
101569	the water will reach each pipe intersection vertex in the order of their shortest distance from the
101570	source. Dijkstra’s algorithm discretizes this continuous process by repeatedly relaxing edges from
101571	a vertex whose minimum weight path estimate is smallest among vertices whose out-going edges
101572	have not yet been relaxed. In order to efficiently find the smallest minimum weight path estimate,
101573	Dijkstra’s algorithm is often presented in terms of a minimum priority queue data structure. Dijk￾stra’s running time then depends on how efficiently the priority queue can perform its supported
101574	operations. Below is Python code for Dijkstra’s algorithm in terms of priority queue operations.
101575	1 def dijkstra(Adj, w, s):
101576	2 d = [float(’inf’) for _ in Adj] # shortest path estimates d(s, v)
101577	3 parent = [None for _ in Adj] # initialize parent pointers
101578	4 d[s], parent[s] = 0, s # initialize source
101579	5 Q = PriorityQueue() # initialize empty priority queue
101580	6 V = len(Adj) # number of vertices
101581	7 for v in range(V): # loop through vertices
101582	8 Q.insert(v, d[v]) # insert vertex-estimate pair
101583	9 for _ in range(V): # main loop
101584	10 u = Q.extract_min() # extract vertex with min estimate
101585	11 for v in Adj[u]: # loop through out-going edges
101586	12 try_to_relax(Adj, w, d, parent, u, v)
101587	13 Q.decrease_key(v, d[v]) # update key of vertex
101588	14 return d, parent
101589	This algorithm follows the same structure as the general relaxation framework. Lines 2-4 initialize
101590	shortest path weight estimates and parent pointers. Lines 5-7 initialize a priority queue with all
101591	vertices from the graph. Lines 8-12 comprise the main loop. Each time the loop is executed, line
101592	9 removes a vertex from the queue, so the queue will be empty at the end of the loop. The vertex
101593	u processed in some iteration of the loop is a vertex from the queue whose shortest path weight
101594	estimate is smallest, from among all vertices not yet removed from the queue. Then, lines 10-11
101595	relax the out-going edges from u as usual. However, since relaxation may reduce the shortest path
101596	weight estimate d(s, v), vertex v’s key in the queue must be updated (if it still exists in the queue);
101597	line 12 accomplishes this update.
101598	2 Recitation 13
101599	Why does Dijkstra’s algorithm compute shortest paths for a graph with non-negative edge weights?
101600	The key observation is that shortest path weight estimate of vertex u equals its actual shortest path
101601	weight d(s, u) = δ(s, u) when u is removed from the priority queue. Then by the upper-bound
101602	property, d(s, u) = δ(s, u) will still hold at termination of the algorithm. A proof of correctness is
101603	described in the lecture notes, and will not be repeated here. Instead, we will focus on analyzing
101604	running time for Dijkstra implemented using different priority queues.
101605	Exercise: Construct a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights, and apply Dijkstra’s algo￾rithm to find shortest paths. Specifically list the key-value pairs stored in the priority queue after
101606	each iteration of the main loop, and highlight edges corresponding to constructed parent pointers.
101607	Priority Queues
101608	An important aspect of Dijkstra’s algorithm is the use of a priority queue. The priority queue
101609	interface used here differs slightly from our presentation of priority queues earlier in the term.
101610	Here, a priority queue maintains a set of key-value pairs, where vertex v is a value and d(s, v) is its
101611	key. Aside from empty initialization, the priority queue supports three operations: insert(val,
101612	key) adds a key-value pair to the queue, extract min() removes and returns a value from the
101613	queue whose key is minimum, and decrease key(val, new key) which reduces the key of
101614	a given value stored in the queue to the provided new key. The running time of Dijkstra depends
101615	on the running times of these operations. Specifically, if Ti, Te, and Td are the respective running
101616	times for inserting a key-value pair, extracting a value with minimum key, and decreasing the key
101617	of a value, the running time of Dijkstra will be:
101618	TDijkstra = O(|V | · Ti + |V | · Te + |E| · Td).
101619	There are many different ways to implement a priority queue, achieving different running times
101620	for each operation. Probably the simplest implementation is to store all the vertices and their
101621	current shortest path estimate in a dictionary. A hash table of size O(|V |) can support expected
101622	constant time O(1) insertion and decrease-key operations, though to find and extract the vertex
101623	with minimum key takes linear time O(|V |). If the vertices are indices into the vertex set with
101624	a linear range, then we can alternatively use a direct access array, leading to worst case O(1)
101625	time insertion and decrease-key, while remaining linear O(|V |) to find and extract the vertex with
101626	minimum key. In either case, the running time for Dijkstra simplifies to:
101627	TDict = O(|V |
101628	2 + |E|).
101629	This is actually quite good! If the graph is dense, |E| = Ω(|V |
101630	2), this implementation is linear in
101631	the size of the input! Below is a Python implementation of Dijkstra using a direct access array to
101632	implement the priority queue.
101633	3 Recitation 13
101634	1 class PriorityQueue: # Hash Table Implementation
101635	2 def __init__(self): # stores keys with unique labels
101636	3 self.A = {}
101637	4
101638	5 def insert(self, label, key): # insert labeled key
101639	6 self.A[label] = key
101640	7
101641	8 def extract_min(self): # return a label with minimum key
101642	9 min_label = None
101643	10 for label in self.A:
101644	11 if (min_label is None) or (self.A[label] < self.A[min_label].key):
101645	12 min_label = label
101646	13 del self.A[min_label]
101647	14 return min_label
101648	15
101649	16 def decrease_key(self, label, key): # decrease key of a given label
101650	17 if (label in self.A) and (key < self.A[label]):
101651	18 self.A[label] = key
101652	If the graph is sparse, |E| = O(|V |), we can speed things up with more sophisticated priority queue
101653	implementations. We’ve seen that a binary min heap can implement insertion and extract-min in
101654	O(log n) time. However, decreasing the key of a value stored in a priority queue requires finding
101655	the value in the heap in order to change its key, which naively could take linear time. However,
101656	this difficulty is easily addressed: each vertex can maintain a pointer to its stored location within
101657	the heap, or the heap can maintain a mapping from values (vertices) to locations within the heap
101658	(you were asked to do this in Problem Set 5). Either solution can support finding a given value
101659	in the heap in constant time. Then, after decreasing the value’s key, one can restore the min heap
101660	property in logarithmic time by re-heapifying the tree. Since a binary heap can support each of the
101661	three operations in O(log |V |) time, the running time of Dijkstra will be:
101662	THeap = O((|V | + |E|)log |V |).
101663	For sparse graphs, that’s O(|V | log |V |)! For graphs in between sparse and dense, there is an even
101664	more sophisticated priority queue implementation using a data structure called a Fibonacci Heap,
101665	which supports amortized O(1) time insertion and decrease-key operations, along with O(log n)
101666	minimum extraction. Thus using a Fibonacci Heap to implement the Dijkstra priority queue leads
101667	to the following worst-case running time:
101668	TFibHeap = O(|V | log |V | + |E|).
101669	We won’t be talking much about Fibonacci Heaps in this class, but they’re theoretically useful for
101670	speeding up Dijkstra on graphs that have a number of edges asymptotically in between linear and
101671	quadratic in the number of graph vertices. You may quote the Fibonacci Heap running time bound
101672	whenever you need to argue the running time of Dijkstra when solving theory questions.

101724	4 Recitation 13
101725	class Item:
101726	def __init__(self, label, key):
101727	self.label, self.key = label, key
101728	class PriorityQueue: # Binary Heap Implementation
101729	def __init__(self): # stores keys with unique labels
101730	self.A = []
101731	self.label2idx = {}
101732	def min_heapify_up(self, c):
101733	if c == 0: return
101734	p = (c - 1) // 2
101735	if self.A[p].key > self.A[c].key:
101736	self.A[c], self.A[p] = self.A[p], self.A[c]
101737	self.label2idx[self.A[c].label] = c
101738	self.label2idx[self.A[p].label] = p
101739	self.min_heapify_up(p)
101740	def min_heapify_down(self, p):
101741	if p >= len(self.A): return
101742	l = 2 * p + 1
101743	r = 2 * p + 2
101744	if l >= len(self.A): l = p
101745	if r >= len(self.A): r = p
101746	c = l if self.A[r].key > self.A[l].key else r
101747	if self.A[p].key > self.A[c].key:
101748	self.A[c], self.A[p] = self.A[p], self.A[c]
101749	self.label2idx[self.A[c].label] = c
101750	self.label2idx[self.A[p].label] = p
101751	self.min_heapify_down(c)
101752	def insert(self, label, key): # insert labeled key
101753	self.A.append(Item(label, key))
101754	idx = len(self.A) - 1
101755	self.label2idx[self.A[idx].label] = idx
101756	self.min_heapify_up(idx)
101757	def extract_min(self): # remove a label with minimum key
101758	self.A[0], self.A[-1] = self.A[-1], self.A[0]
101759	self.label2idx[self.A[0].label] = 0
101760	del self.label2idx[self.A[-1].label]
101761	min_label = self.A.pop().label
101762	self.min_heapify_down(0)
101763	return min_label
101764	def decrease_key(self, label, key): # decrease key of a given label
101765	if label in self.label2idx:
101766	idx = self.label2idx[label]
101767	if key < self.A[idx].key:
101768	self.A[idx].key = key
101769	self.min_heapify_up(idx)
101794	5 Recitation 13
101795	Fibonacci Heaps are not actually used very often in practice as it is more complex to implement,
101796	and results in larger constant factor overhead than the other two implementations described above.
101797	When the number of edges in the graph is known to be at most linear (e.g., planar or bounded
101798	degree graphs) or at least quadratic (e.g. complete graphs) in the number of vertices, then using a
101799	binary heap or dictionary respectively will perform as well asymptotically as a Fibonacci Heap.

101802	Exercise: CIA officer Mary Cathison needs to drive to meet with an informant across an unwel￾come city. Some roads in the city are equipped with government surveillance cameras, and Mary
101803	will be detained if cameras from more than one road observe her car on the way to her informant.
101804	Mary has a map describing the length of each road and the locations and ranges of surveillance
101805	cameras. Help Mary find the shortest drive to reach her informant, being seen by at most one
101806	surveillance camera along the way.
101807	Solution: Construct a graph having two vertices (v, 0) and (v, 1) for every road intersection v
101808	within the city. Vertex (v,i) represents arriving at intersection v having already been spotted by
101809	exactly i camera(s). For each road from intersection u to v: add two directed edges from (u, 0) to
101810	(v, 0) and from (u, 1) to (v, 1) if traveling on the road will not be visible by a camera; and add one
101811	directed edge from (u, 0) to (v, 1) if traveling on the road will be visible. If s is Mary’s start location
101812	and t is the location of the informant, any path from (s, 0) to (t, 0) or (t, 1) in the constructed graph
101813	will be a path visible by at most one camera. Let n be the number of road intersections and m be the
101814	number of roads in the network. Assuming lengths of roads are positive, use Dijkstra’s algorithm
101815	to find the shortest such path in O(m +n log n) time using a Fibonacci Heap for Dijkstra’s priority
101816	queue. Alternatively, since the road network is likely planar and/or bounded degree, it may be
101817	safe to assume that m = O(n), so a binary heap could be used instead to find a shortest path in
101818	O(n log n) time.

103174	Single Source Shortest Paths Review
103175	We’ve learned four algorithms to solve the single source shortest paths (SSSP) problem; they are
103176	listed in the table below. Then, to solve shortest paths problems, you must first define or construct
103177	a graph related to your problem, and then running an SSSP algorithm on that graph in a way that
103178	solves your problem. Generally, you will want to use the fastest SSSP algorithm that solves your
103179	problem. Bellman-Ford applies to any weighted graph but is the slowest of the four, so we prefer
103180	the other algorithms whenever they are applicable.
103181	|V | · |E|
103182	We presented these algorithms with respect to the SSSP problem, but along the way, we also
103183	showed how to use these algorithms to solve other problems. For example, we can also count
103184	connected components in a graph using Full-DFS or Full-BFS, topologically sort vertices in a
103185	DAG using DFS, and detect negative weight cycles using Bellman-Ford.
103186	All Pairs Shortest Paths
103187	Given a weighted graph G = (V, E,w), the (weighted) All Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP) problem
103188	asks for the minimum weight δ(u, v) of any path from u to v for every pair of vertices u, v ∈ V . To
103189	make the problem a little easier, if there exists a negative weight cycle in G, our algorithm is not
103190	required to return any output. A straight-forward way to solve this problem is to reduce to solving
103191	an SSSP problem |V | times, once from each vertex in V . This strategy is actually quite good for
103192	special types of graphs! For example, suppose we want to solve ASPS on an unweighted graph
103193	that is sparse (i.e. |E| = O(|V |)). Running BFS from each vertex takes O(|V |
103194	2) time. Since
103195	we need to return a value δ(u, v) for each pair of vertices, any ASPS algorithm requires at least
103196	Ω(V 2) time, so this algorithm is optimal for graphs that are unweighted and sparse. However,
103197	for general graphs, possibly containing negative weight edges, running Bellman-Ford |V | times is
103198	quite slow, O(|V |
103199	2|E|), a factor of |E| larger than the output. By contrast, if we have a graph that
103200	only has non-negative weights, applying Dijkstra |V | times takes O(|V |
103201	2 log |V | + |V ||E|) time.
103202	On a sparse graph, running Dijkstra |V | times is only a log |V | factor larger than the output, while
103203	|V | times Bellman-Ford is a linear |V | factor larger. Is it possible to solve the APSP problem on
103204	general weighted graphs faster than O(|V |
103205	2|E|)?
103207	Recitation 14 2
103208	Johnson’s Algorithm
103209	The idea behind Johnson’s Algorithm is to reduce the ASPS problem on a graph with arbitrary
103210	edge weights to the ASPS problem on a graph with non-negative edge weights. The algorithm
103211	does this by re-weighting the edges in the original graph to non-negative values in such a way so
103212	that shortest paths in the re-weighted graph are also shortest paths in the original graph. Then find￾ing shortest paths in the re-weighted graph using |V | times Dijkstra will solve the original problem.
103213	How can we re-weight edges in a way that preserves shortest paths? Johnson’s clever idea is to
103214	assign each vertex v a real number h(v), and change the weight of each edge (a, b) from w(a, b) to
103215	w0
103216	(a, b) = w(a, b) + h(a) − h(b), to form a new weight graph G0 = (V, E,w0
103217	).
103218	Claim: A shortest path (v1, v2, . . . , vk) in G0 is also a shortest path in G from v1 to vk. Pk−1 Proof. Let w(π) = i=1 w(vi, vi+1) be the weight of path π in G. Then weight of π in G0 is:
103219	k−1 k−1
103220	Xw0
103221	(vi, vi+1) = X w(vi, vi+1) + h(vi) − h(vi+1)
103222	i=1 i=1
103223	! ! ! k−1 k−1 k−1
103224	X X X = w(vi, vi+1) + h(vi) − h(vi+1) = w(π) + h(v1) − h(vk).
103225	i=1 i=1 i=1
103226	So, since each path from v1 to vk is increased by the same number h(v1) − h(vk), shortest paths
103227	remain shortest.
103228	It remains to find a vertex assignment function h, for which all edge weights w0
103229	(a, b) in the modi-
103230	fied graph are non-negative. Johnson’s defines h in the following way: add a new node x to G with
103231	a directed edge from x to v for each vertex v ∈ V to construct graph G∗, letting h(v) = δ(x, v).
103232	This assignment of h ensures that w0
103233	(a, b) ≥ 0 for every edge (a, b).
103234	Claim: If h(v) = δ(x, v) and h(v) is finite, then w0
103235	(a, b) = w(a, b) + h(a) − h(b) ≥ 0 for every
103236	edge (a, b) ∈ E.
103237	Proof. The claim is equivalent to claiming δ(x, b) ≤ w(a, b) +δ(x, a) for every edge (a, b) ∈ E,
103238	i.e. the minimum weight of any path from x to b in G∗ is not greater than the minimum weight of
103239	any path from x to a than traversing the edge from a to b, which is true by definition of minimum
103240	weight. (This is simply a restatement of the triangle inequality.)
103241	Johnson’s algorithm computes h(v) = δ(x, v), negative minimum weight distances from the added
103242	node x, using Bellman-Ford. If δ(x, v) = −∞ for any vertex v, then there must be a negative
103243	weight cycle in the graph, and Johnson’s can terminate as no output is required. Otherwise, John￾son’s can re-weight the edges of G to w0
103244	(a, b) = w(a, b) +h(a)−h(b) ≥ 0 into G0 containing only
103245	positive edge weights. Since shortest paths in G0 are shortest paths in G, we can run Dijkstra |V |
103246	times on G0 to find a single source shortest paths distances δ0
103247	(u, v) from each vertex u in G0
103248	. Then
103249	we can compute each δ(u, v) by setting it to δ0
103250	(u, v)−δ(x, u)+δ(x, y). Johnson’s takes O(|V ||E|)
103251	time to run Bellman-Ford, and O(|V |(|V | log |V | + |E|)) time to run Dijkstra |V | times, so this
103252	algorithm runs in O(|V |
103253	2 log |V | + |V ||E|) time, asymptotically better than O(|V |
103254	2|E|).

103424	Problem 6-1. [15 points] Dijkstra Practice
103425	Consider weighted graph G = (V, E,w) below, which is acyclic and has nonnegative edge weights.
103426	(a) Run both DAG Relaxation and Dijkstra on G from vertex
103427	a. Each algorithm tries to relax every edge (u, v) ∈ E,
103428	a b c
103429	d e f
103430	2 1
103431	but does so in a different order. For each algorithm, write
103432	down a list of all edges in relaxation order: the order 1 2
103433	3 1 the algorithm tries to relax them. If there is ambiguity 6
103434	on which vertex or outgoing adjacency to process next,
103435	process them in alphabetical order. 0 2
103436	(b) List δ(a, v) for each v ∈ V (via either algorithm).
103437	Solution: Relaxation order is unique for both algorithms.
103438	DAG Relaxation: [(a, b),(a, d),(d, b),(d, e),(b, c),(b, e),(b, f),(e, f),(f, c)]
103439	Dijkstra: [(a, b),(a, d),(b, c),(b, e),(b, f),(f, c),(e, f),(d, b),(d, e)]
103440	v a b c d e f
103441	δ(a, v) 0 2 3 6 5 4

103447	Problem 6-2. [10 points] Short Circuits
103448	Given a weighted directed graph G = (V, E,w) and vertex s ∈ V , with the property that, for
103449	every vertex v ∈ V , some minimum-weight path from s to v traverses at most k edges, describe an
103450	algorithm to find the shortest-path weight from s to each v ∈ V in O(|V | + k|E|) time.
103451	Solution: Since this graph may contain cycles and negative weights, at first it seems we do not
103452	know how to do better than Bellman-Ford. Fortunately, the problem gives us an additional re￾striction: that a shortest path to each vertex traverses few edges. Since layer k0 of the duplicated
103453	2 Problem Set 6
103454	graph G0 of Bellman-Ford corresponds to shortest paths to that vertex using at most k0 edges, our
103455	approach will be to modify Bellman-Ford to only construct the duplicated graph layers incremen￾tally, relax edges into the new layers online to compute k0
103456	-edge shortest paths, and then stop when
103457	k0
103458	-edge shortest path distance do not change from layer to layer.
103459	Specifically, rather than creating the duplicated graph G0 all at once and then running DAG Re￾laxation, we begin with G0 only containing the first layer (v0 for v ∈ V ) and δ initialized with
103460	first-layer distances δ(s0, v0) = ∞ for v ∈ V , except for δ(s0, s0) = 0.
103461	Then for i starting at 0, assume for induction that G0 contains layers 0 to i and δ(s0, vj ) have been
103462	computed for all v ∈ V and j ∈ {0, . . . , i}, append layer i + 1 by adding vertices vi+1 for v ∈ V
103463	and associated edges from layer i. This new layer cannot effect distances in previous layers (since
103464	the new layer comes later in the topological order. So, continue DAG Relaxation by relaxing the
103465	new edges out of the vertices in layer i, which correctly computes δ(s0, vi+1) for all v ∈ V .
103466	Since a shortest path from s to each vertex uses at most k edges, the distance δ(s, v) equals the
103467	k0
103468	-edge distance δk0(s, v) = δ(s0, vk0) for every k0 ≥ k. Thus, as soon as δ(s0, vk0) = δ(s0, vk0+1)
103469	for all v ∈ V , then k0 = k and we can terminate by outputting δ(s, v) = δ(s0, vk) for each v ∈ V .
103470	Since every vertex is reachable from s, |V | = O(|E|), and since we only construct k + 1 layers
103471	of G0 before finding two equal layers, and each layer takes at most O(|E|) time to process, this
103472	algorithm runs in O(k|E|) time (which is also O(|V | + k|E|)). The |V | was originally provided
103473	for this problem to allow the input to include disconnected graph, where an initial single-source
103474	reachability algorithm could restrict to the subset of the graph reachable from s; but this term is no
103475	longer relevant for connected input graphs.
103476	Rubric:
103477	• 6 points for description of a correct algorithm that runs in O(k|E|) time
103478	• 2 points for a correct argument of correctness
103479	• 2 points for a correct argument of running time
103480	• Partial credit may be awarded
103481	• Max 4 points for a correct O(|V ||E|)-time algorithm
103482	Problem 6-3. [20 points] Dynamite Detonation
103483	Superspy Bames Jond is fleeing the alpine mountain lair of Silvertoe, the evil tycoon. Bames has
103484	stolen a pair of skis and a trail map listing the mountain’s clearings and slopes (n in total), and she
103485	wants to ski from the clearing L by the lair to a clearing S where a snowmobile awaits.
103486	• Each clearing ci ∈ C has an integer elevation ei above sea level.
103487	• Each slope (ci, cj , `ij ) connects a pair of clearings ci and cj with a monotonic trail (strictly
103488	decreasing or increasing in elevation) with positive integer length `ij . Bames doesn’t have
103489	time to ski uphill, so she will only traverse slopes so as to decrease her elevation.
103490	3 Problem Set 6
103491	• On her way up the mountain, Bames laced the mountain with dynamite at known locations
103492	CD ⊂ C. Detonating the dynamite will immediately change the elevation of clearings ci ∈
103493	CD by a known amount, from ei to a lower elevation ei
103494	0 < ei. The detonator exists at clearing
103495	D ∈ C (where there is no dynamite). If she reaches clearing D, she can choose to detonate
103496	the dynamite before continuing on.
103497	Given Bames’ map and dynamite data, describe an O(n)-time algorithm to find the minimum
103498	distance she must ski to reach the snowmobile (possibly detonating the dynamite along the way).
103499	Solution: We can model the mountain as a DAG of trails that Bames may ski downhill, both
103500	before and after possible detonation. Construct a graph G1 with a vertex for every clearing and a
103501	directed edge for every slope pointing to the lower clearing; remove any slopes that do not change
103502	height along the way (since Bames will not traverse the slope in either direction). Construct a
103503	second graph G2 in the same way as G1, except using the modified heights ei
103504	0 that represents the
103505	state of the mountain after the dynamite explodes. In both graphs, we weight edges by the length
103506	lij of the corresponding slope. Connect G1 and G2 into a single graph G by adding one directed
103507	edge from node D1 in graph G1 to node D2 in graph G2 with weight 0 (taking this edge represents
103508	blowing up the dynamite); and add a supernode T that has incoming edges of zero weight from
103509	nodes S1 in graph G1 and S2 in graph G2 (representing reaching S by either not detonating or
103510	detonating the dynamite respectively).
103511	We can now run DAG Relaxation from node L1 in graph G to the supernode T; the shortest such
103512	path is the minimum distance to get from L to S, with or without detonation, while respecting that
103513	Bames only decreases her elevation. Graph G has O(n) vertices and edges, so DAG Relaxation
103514	runs in O(n) time, as desired.
103515	Rubric:
103516	• 6 points for construction of a graph that can be used to solve the problem
103517	• 3 points for description of a correct algorithm
103518	• 2 points for a correct argument of correctness
103519	• 3 points for a correct argument of running time
103520	• 6 points if correct algorithm is efficient, i.e., O(n)-time
